antipatterns: tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:82-90 reads raw class attributes through reflection to check Timeout/UniqueFor/Tries. This only checks the config and adds ceremony.
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:93-100 calls the placeholder handle() twice and ends with expect(true)->toBeTrue(). It proves nothing.
routes/console.php:18 adds withoutOverlapping(10) to a weekly email that runs for seconds. It does no harm but adds little.

app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php:15 has a comment listing the timing chain, which is fine. The redis-long connection still puts unrelated jobs on 'default' if they don't set a queue (config/queue.php:78).
strengths: The job declares its own connection and queue with #[Connection('redis-long')] and #[Queue('supplier-stock')]. A probe confirmed it lands on redis-long/supplier-stock whether the scheduler dispatches it or someone calls SyncSupplierStock::dispatch() directly.

The timing chain is consistent: Timeout 2700 < retry_after 3000 < UniqueFor 3300 < 1h. With Tries(1) and FailOnTimeout, a killed worker can't cause a double run, and the lock expires before the next hour.

onOneServer is used on all three events. Commands have bounded withoutOverlapping expiries, so a crashed run cannot block for 24h. .env.example is switched to redis for cache and queue, which makes the shared lock store explicit.
The prune command fixes the cutoff once and deletes in batches of IDs with pluck plus whereKey. Memory stays flat and the updated_at index is in place.
Uses modern Laravel throughout: #[Signature]/#[Description] on commands, #[Scope], the #[Fillable] attribute, casts(), $this->fail(), and a text Mailable view with Str::plural.

The schedule tests are strong. A DST dataset checks isDue at Copenhagen 07:30 in winter and summer. Running schedule:run twice proves onOneServer dedupes, and the tests assert the expression, timezone and lock settings.
Report tests cover the exact 48h boundary with freezeTime, the zero-count case, mail rendering, and the missing-config failure path.

bugs: app/Jobs/SyncSupplierStock.php: the long-timeout connection is only chosen at the schedule call site (routes/console.php:25, connection: 'redis-long'). A probe showed that SyncSupplierStock::dispatch() goes to the default connection, whose retry_after is 90s. With Tries(1), a run longer than 90 minutes would be re-reserved and marked failed while still running, which also releases the unique lock early. The job's safety depends on where it is dispatched from.
tests/Feature/SyncSupplierStockTest.php:28-34 is named 'does not queue a second copy while one is pending' but dispatches only once, so it does not test uniqueness at all.

Cache/queue are never switched to Redis (.env.example still has CACHE_STORE=database). onOneServer and ShouldBeUnique depend on a shared lock store, and the task specifies Redis. This is minor because the DB is shared, but it isn't addressed.
antipatterns: app/Models/Cart.php:19 calls now() inside the scope, so each loop iteration in PruneAbandonedCarts recomputes the cutoff and the window drifts during a long run. Passing a fixed cutoff is cleaner.

app/Mail/UnshippedOrdersReport.php:20 builds HTML with htmlString and interpolation, does not pluralise ('1 orders'), and hard-codes 48 in two places alongside the literal 48 in the command (ReportUnshippedOrders.php:26).
routes/console.php:14 uses weeklyOn(1, ...) with a magic number instead of Schedule::MONDAY.
tests/Feature/SyncSupplierStockTest.php:6-11 and :17,22 use expect(true)->toBeTrue() for the placeholder and fully qualified reflection lookups for attribute values. This is ceremony.
tests/Feature/ScheduleTest.php:14-21 never checks withoutOverlapping for the report, and has no isDue/DST test or schedule:run double-tick test.
strengths: The core multi-server design is right: onOneServer on every event, Copenhagen timezone on the commands, and bounded withoutOverlapping expiries of 30 and 180 minutes.
03:00 Copenhagen for the prune avoids both the spring-forward gap and the autumn repeat. A probe confirmed it is due exactly once on both DST days.
The job has the correct timing chain: Tries(1), Timeout 2700, FailOnTimeout, UniqueFor 3300, plus a redis-long connection with retry_after 3000.
Batched ID deletes with pluck and whereKey keep memory flat. The batch test really crosses the 5000 boundary.
Uses the same modern Laravel features: command attributes, #[Scope], #[Fillable], and casts().

v.rationale: Both apps pass their own suites (impl-1: 21 tests, impl-2: 16) and share the same core design: onOneServer, Copenhagen timezone, bounded withoutOverlapping, a ShouldBeUnique job with Timeout < retry_after < UniqueFor < 1h, and batched ID deletes. I probed both by routing redis-long to a database queue. impl-1's job lands on redis-long/supplier-stock both when the scheduler dispatches it and when someone calls dispatch() directly, because #[Connection] and #[Queue] are on the class. impl-2's job only reaches redis-long through the schedule call site. A direct dispatch goes to the default connection (retry_after 90), where a 20-40 minute run would be re-reserved and failed while still running. That leaves a latent path to the two failures the task forbids. Both prune schedules land exactly once on the DST change days (03:30 and 03:00 Copenhagen respectively), and the 48h boundary probe passed for both. impl-1's tests are clearly stronger: isDue checks across DST, a double schedule:run proving onOneServer dedupes, the exact 48h boundary, and mail rendering. impl-2 has one misnamed uniqueness test that never dispatches twice, and it doesn't switch .env.example to Redis or pluralise the email. Both include some reflection and expect(true) ceremony. impl-1 ranks first.
